subject: Post-call: Streaming performance profile & decision framework
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Streaming performance profile & decision framework

Thanks again for the time today — good convo. Below is a concise recap so we have the same picture and concrete next steps. Please correct anything I mis-captured.

Call highlights / current pain points
- Repeated p95 spikes during peak ingest windows (11am–1pm PT) that result in client-side timeouts and degraded streaming UX.
- Streaming responses often arrive in multiple short chunks with 700–1200ms gaps between first and last chunk; users see a flickering experience.
- Current infra: in-house Triton + K8s with autoscaling; they do not use persistent KV caching across requests and have limited multiplexing.
- Concurrency requirement: expected steady concurrency of ~300 sessions, burst up to 1.2k for short windows. Typical turn length ~40–80 tokens, some long-form up to 700 tokens.

Success criteria (what Finlytics needs):
1) First-token p95 <= 350ms for streaming sessions at steady concurrency (300).
2) End-to-end response p95 <= 900ms for 95% of 40–80 token responses; long-form can be higher but must not degrade UI.
3) Stable UX for bursts up to 1.2k concurrent sessions without >5% error rate.

Hypothesis / how Redwood can help (sketch):
- Prefix/KV caching + short-path kernel selection for common prompt families to lower first-token latency.
- Continuous batching tuned by per-customer request arrival patterns to allow low latency at steady-state but aggressive multiplexing during bursts.
- Canary rollout using a lightweight model-variant and automatic fallback to baseline model if p95 exceeds threshold.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you share an anonymized 48-hour trace (timestamps, request sizes, sample trace IDs, and percentiles per minute)? We only need metadata to reproduce arrival patterns — not content. (Attachment: current_traffic_snapshot.csv is an example of the CSV schema.)
2) Please confirm whether any requests travel via a region outside US (GDPR/not relevant) — you mentioned all traffic is US-only.
3) We will run a quick internal decision framework and return an initial MOP (method-of-play) + cost estimates by EOD Friday Aug 13.

Planned Redwood deliverables
- 1-page decision framework mapping recommended knobs (batch size, cache TTL, model variant) to p95/cost tradeoffs.
- MOP draft for an initial pilot (3–4 week run) including telemetry hooks and rollback criteria.

Attachments referenced: current_traffic_snapshot.csv, redwood_sla_framework.pdf (decision framework draft).

If that all looks right, I’ll open a shared Drive folder and Ben / Monica will start internal sizing. Suggested short sync: Tue Aug 17 to walk through traces and the MOP.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_sla_framework.pdf)
From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Streaming performance profile & decision framework

Appreciate the write-up — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications:
- The 11am–1pm spike is primarily driven by batch uploads from our analytics pipeline (not user-driven), so the request size distribution during that window skews larger.
- We can produce a 48-hour anonymized trace; will scrub payloads and provide timestamps, request token counts, and request IDs.
- We use a single US region (us-west-2) only.

We’re good with your proposed approach. Two asks from our side:
1) Can the decision framework include an explicit rollback SLO (e.g., rollback if first-token p95 > 500ms for 10 consecutive minutes)?
2) We’d like a rough monthly spend estimate for the pilot at both steady and burst scenarios (ballpark fine).

We’ll upload the traces to the Drive link you suggested by EOD Thursday Aug 13.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
CTO, Finlytics
(Attachment: example_trace_manifest.json)
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Streaming performance profile & decision framework

Forwarding Samir’s confirmation — they’ll drop traces by Thu (Aug 13). Internal asks below so we can move fast: please keep replies internal unless you need product/legal to engage.

Internal action items (owner & ETA)
- Ben: produce a 1-page MOP skeleton with rollback criteria and canary thresholds (ETA: 48 hours). See MOP-template.docx.
- Monica: preliminary cost delta for a 3-week pilot (steady vs burst) and an ops-runbook estimate (hours + on-call ramp) (ETA: 72 hours).
- Avery: assemble decision framework PDF and proposed pilot timeline; coordinate Drive folder and schedule Tues Aug 17 sync.

Notes for engineering scope (Ben / Monica):
- We should include a short experiment to validate prefix caching for the top 5 prompt families. If effective, that will drop first-token p95 substantially.
- Verify model-variant latency characteristics for 40–80 token vs 400–700 token tails; include GPU selection guidance (A100 vs H100-like behaviors).
- Include telemetry keys: request_id, arrival_ms, model_variant, batch_size, first_token_ms, last_token_ms. Samir said they can annotate request IDs.

Attachments to attach to the shared Drive: MOP-template.docx, redwood_sla_framework.pdf (decision framework draft).

I’ll prep the Drive folder and invite Samir/Priya once the MOP skeleton is ready.

-Avery
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Streaming performance profile & decision framework

Sounds good — I’ll take the MOP skeleton. Quick confirmation items:
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with 15 minute observation windows and automatic rollback on first-token p95 > 500ms for two consecutive windows.
- Pilot infra: propose reserved pool of capacity sized for steady 300 concurrency + configured burst headroom via autoscaler (we’ll size exact numbers after seeing traces).
- I’ll include a short ops checklist for quick recovery steps (drain nodes, fallback to smaller variant, enable caching TTL to 0 to force baseline behavior).

ETA: skeleton MOP by EOD Wed Aug 14 (will attach to the Drive).

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: MOP-template.docx)
